patch:
diff --git a/pipeline/ingest.py b/pipeline/ingest.py
index be24468..64846a3 100644
--- a/pipeline/ingest.py
+++ b/pipeline/ingest.py
@@ -59,8 +59,11 @@ def accept(raw_records, settings):
             out.drop(constants.DROP_UNKNOWN_CHANNEL)
             continue
 
-        # Quality gate. VALID_FLAGS is written in rev A's lower-case spelling.
-        flag = rec.get(constants.FLAG_KEY)
+        # Quality gate. VALID_FLAGS is written in rev A's lower-case spelling,
+        # so the flag must be folded through normalize.canonical_flag() first --
+        # rev B firmware emits OK/WARN upper-case (docs/firmware_notes.md), and
+        # comparing those raw never matches, silently dropping half the fleet.
+        flag = normalize.canonical_flag(rec.get(constants.FLAG_KEY))
         if flag not in constants.VALID_FLAGS:
             out.drop(constants.DROP_BAD_FLAG)
             continue
prompt:
The nightly telemetry roll-up in this repository is failing. Running it:

    python3 run.py data/samples.jsonl

crashes with:

    File "pipeline/stats.py", line 52, in summarise
        mean = total / len(window.values)
    ZeroDivisionError: division by zero

Operations have also been unhappy with this report for a while: the sample
counts it prints look lower than the volume the fleet is actually sending, but
nobody has pinned that down.

Fix it. When you are done, `python3 run.py data/samples.jsonl` must complete
successfully AND the report it prints must account for every usable sample in
the input file — not merely avoid crashing.

Do not change `data/samples.jsonl`, and do not change the output format: the
report's line shapes are consumed downstream and are part of the contract.
title: the roll-up crashes, and the cause is four modules upstream
